chunks: the neck is free from the loop, and the spirit is unfettered, [providing time] for seeking guidance, ease of the body, assembly in crowds, respite for the remainder [of life], opportunity of acting by will, reprieve for repentance, and expansion of the sphere [of action], before narrowness and distress, fear and weakness, and before the arrival of the awaited [death], and the seizure by the Almighty, the Powerful.

key_terms.الْخِنَاقُ: the neck (metaphor for the noose of death)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by 'the neck is free from the loop' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the *Gharra*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) utilizes vivid metaphors of released spirits and loosened shackles to emphasize the transient nature of worldly freedom as a divine opportunity for *tawbah* (repentance). This exhortation reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *barakah* (blessing) in time, urging believers to act before the 'unexpected arrival' of death (*al-mawt al-muntazar*) and the final accounting. The text serves as a spiritual wake-up call, linking physical vitality directly to the urgency of preparing for the Hereafter.

en.sayed-ali-raza: since the neck is free from the loop, and spirit is also unfettered, now you have time for seeking guidance; you are in ease of body; you can assemble in crowds, the rest of life is before you; you have opportunity of acting by will; there is opportunity for repentance, and peaceful circumstances. (But you should act) before you are overtaken by narrow circumstances and distress, or fear and weakness, before the approach of the awaited death and before seizure by the Almighty, the Powerful.
